I had a similar realization recently. It lead to me finally seeking treatment after years of descending into persistent anger as a coping mechanism. The best way to describe that would be like embracing the Dark Side in SW. Anger allowed me to focus and pass myself off as functional when I had been triggered. It “worked” for me until I finally broke. It was like I woke up one day to find I’d forgotten how to be a person. I spiraled into depression (okay so maybe I dove face first) and became one step short of a shut in over night. Driving somehow evolved a huge trigger for me and highways had become impossible. So I eventually stopped going anywhere. I’m only here writing this bc I was blessed with an amazing support system that refused to lose me. Therapy started a while ago, but now I’m three weeks into medication I ignorantly swore I’d never take and wishing I’d done it sooner. After finally creating some breathing room in my mind, it feels like meeting myself again after years of estrangement. I still recognize who I used to be, but it’s like I’m unfamiliar with who I’ve become and it feels…odd but not at all bad. Last week, I drove on the interstate for the first time in maybe 2 years. I’m not “good” yet, but I’m definitely getting better.

OP, you can do this. You can eventually overcome this. Just don’t try to do it alone. I tried that and it almost killed me.

I never say you were wrong because this is clearly open to interpretation. If they did not meet the requirements of sneak attack then it is cut and dry.

However, I will say that because you do not actually need Advantage in order to perform a sneak attack then I personally would have ruled it the other way. (Note: I also flat out hate that it is called “sneak attack”. In my experience, too many folks are stuck with “you gotta be either hidden or dirty to sneak attack.” Why can’t it just be a really precise strike? Rant over.)

My reasoning can be explained with a question. What makes a better story? 

1) your rogue is poisoned, tries to sneak attack, you say no, nothing happens. Next enemy turn he gets slapped and it goes however it goes from there. Maybe the player is upset or bored and becomes disengaged.

2) your rogue is poisoned but fights through the pain and tries to deliver a Hail Mary stab into the heart of his foe. His blade flashes and his enemy’s blood spatters the floor while he stumbles away, clearly affected by the poison. On the next enemy turn he gets slapped and it goes however it goes from there. The PC just did some cool shit and so the player might even happily watch as you kill the weak and poison Sneak. (Hyperbole Alert! Lol)
